subject: SEM with several latent variables and one observed and ordered dependent variable

messages.author: 98f3f183888e9919
messages.subject: SEM with several latent variables and one observed and ordered dependent variable
parts:
Hi,


I’m running a SEM model with 4 latent variables (L1, L2, L3, L4) which are thought to affect an observed ordered (binary) physical activity, PA, in a population.


Model <- ‘

L1=~Q1+Q2+Q3

L2=~Q4+Q5+Q6+Q7

L3=~Q8+Q9

L4=~Q10+Q11+Q12

# Regression coefficients

PA ~ a*L1 + b*L2+ f*L3 + d*L4

L2~c*L1

L4~e*L3

‘

If I run above model, lavaan treats PA as an additional indicator for each latent variable and estimate a loading correspond to each latent variable. My guess is that this model specification can’t be correct. Am I right?

To overcome this issue, I thought to define a new latent variable L5 (endogenous) and link the PA as its only indicator, that is,

 

Model <- ‘

L1=~Q1+Q2+Q3

L2=~Q4+Q5+Q6+Q7

L3=~Q8+Q9

L4=~Q10+Q11+Q12

L5 =~ PA

# Regression coefficients

L5 ~ a*L1 + b*L2+ f*L3 + d*L4

L2~c*L1

L4~e*L3

# Covariance effect

L5 ~~0*L5    # to force its variance equal zero.

‘


fit <- sem(Model, data=mydata, estimator="WLSMV", ordered="PA")


 

Will appreciate if anyone can help.


Regards,

Ali

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: SEM with several latent variables and one observed and ordered dependent variable
parts:
Ali--
     Whether the criterion binary variable is dependent on the 4 factors or is an indicator of the 4 factors, the statistical model should be exactly the same.  Software may impose differences, but there is no statistical difference.
     Your other approach would work, except . . . to establish equality between PA and L5, you want to force PA's residual variance to 0, not L5's residual variance.  The residual variance of PA says that there is a part of PA that is separate from L5, and I do not think this is what you want.  Leave L5's residual variance free--this is the part of PA not explained by the 4 predictor factors.  But then you should find that R2 for L5 in the second model is equal to R2 for PA in the first model.
      If PA is binary, make sure that your regression is taking account of the special character of the dependent variable.
--Ed Rigdon

messages.subject: Re: SEM with several latent variables and one observed and ordered dependent variable
parts:
Ali--
Yes, precisely . . . PA~~0*PA implies 0 residual variance for PA, making it equivalent to the factor, L5, that PA loads on.
--Ed Rigdon
